label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Scarcity and Opportunity Cost

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Scarcity refers to the situation in which the resources available are not enough to satisfy all people's wants.

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Scarcity concerns whether resources are sufficient relative to people's wants, not whether their physical amount is absolutely small.

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: The opportunity cost of a choice is the value of the highest-valued option forgone.

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Four-step method: state the choice and decision moment; identify the scarce resources required; identify and state the value of the highest-valued option forgone.

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Full cost is the opportunity cost. It is the value of the best alternative uses of all resources necessarily forgone in making a choice.

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Explicit cost: money expenditure made as a result of the current choice, such as ticket payment.

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Implicit cost: value of the best alternative use of self-owned resources or receipts forgone.

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Full cost = explicit cost + implicit cost.

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Three opportunity-cost traps: benefit trap, ranking trap, past-payment trap.

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Benefit trap: a rise in the value of the chosen option does not by itself change its opportunity cost.

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Ranking trap: a changed preference order or new option matters only if it changes the highest-valued option forgone.

label: Scarcity & Cost
text: Past-payment trap: only options available at the decision moment can be forgone.

label: Interest
text: Interest and Time Preference

label: Interest
text: To borrowers, interest is the cost of earlier availability of resources.

label: Interest
text: To lenders, interest is the compensation for deferred availability of resources.

label: Interest
text: Positive time preference: people generally prefer the same amount of the same good earlier rather than later.

label: Interest
text: Interest can exist even without borrowing: choosing to buy later means delaying the use of money.

label: Interest
text: Interest exists in every economy that has scarcity, including a barter economy without money or inflation.

label: Allocation
text: Allocation and Economic Systems

label: Allocation
text: Scarcity forces a rule for deciding who gets what.

label: Allocation
text: Price competition is a type of competition based on users' willingness or ability to pay.

label: Allocation
text: Non-price competition is a type of competition based on criterion other than willingness or ability to pay.

label: Allocation
text: Economic good: quantity is insufficient for all wants. Free good: quantity is sufficient for all wants.

label: Allocation
text: Free-of-charge is not the same as free good.

label: Allocation
text: Traditional economy tackles the three basic economic problems mainly by customs and traditions.

label: Allocation
text: Planned or command economy tackles the three basic economic problems mainly by government decisions.

label: Allocation
text: Market economy tackles the three basic economic problems mainly by the market mechanism.

label: Allocation
text: Private property rights: exclusive right to use, exclusive right to receive income, and the right to transfer.

label: Circular Flow
text: Circular Flow and Specialization

label: Circular Flow
text: Four flows form one circular system: two real flows and two money flows in opposite directions.

label: Circular Flow
text: Product market: final goods and services are traded.

label: Circular Flow
text: Factor market: factor services supplied by the owners of factors of production are traded.

label: Circular Flow
text: Real flow is the flow of goods and services. Money flow is the flow of monetary income and expenditure.

label: Circular Flow
text: Market value in production = income generated in production = expenditure on final output.

label: Circular Flow
text: Specialize according to lower opportunity cost. Comparative advantage guides who produces what.

label: Circular Flow
text: Positive statement is a claim about the objective world that is refutable by facts.

label: Circular Flow
text: Normative statement is a claim involving value judgement.

label: Demand & Supply
text: Demand, Supply and Equilibrium

label: Demand & Supply
text: Demand is the set of quantities of a good that consumers are willing and able to buy at all corresponding prices over a period of time.

label: Demand & Supply
text: Law of demand: an increase in price of a good will result in a decrease in its quantity demanded, and vice versa, other things being constant.

label: Demand & Supply
text: Quantity demanded is the amount buyers are willing and able to buy at one particular price.

label: Demand & Supply
text: Market demand is the combined demand of all consumers, found by horizontal summation.

label: Demand & Supply
text: Relative price of X in terms of Y = normal price of X / normal price of Y.

label: Demand & Supply
text: Supply is the set of quantities of a good that producers are willing and able to sell at all corresponding prices.

label: Demand & Supply
text: Law of supply: an increase in the price of a good will result in an increase in its quantity supplied.

label: Demand & Supply
text: Market equilibrium: quantity demanded equals quantity supplied and there is no tendency for the price to change.

label: Demand & Supply
text: Excess demand: Qd > Qs. Excess supply: Qs > Qd. Quantity transacted = min(Qd, Qs).

label: Exam Skills
text: Exam Skills

label: Exam Skills
text: Definition question: write the opportunity cost of a choice is the value of the highest-valued option forgone.

label: Exam Skills
text: Identify-and-explain question: state the choice and highest-valued available option forgone; state the value of that option as the cost.

label: Exam Skills
text: Answer frame for cost changes: before the change, the cost is the value of ___. The change affects or does not affect the resources required, the value of this option, or which option is highest-valued.

label: Exam Skills
text: Whenever an economic variable changes ask: which option becomes more or less attractive? Which scarce resource is affected? What is now the highest-valued alternative forgone?

label: Exam Skills
text: Never infer free good from a zero money price. Compare quantity available with all wants.
